title: Reverse a List
statement:
Store a list of numbers and give them back in reverse order.

The first line is a whole number `n`, at least 1. The second line holds `n` integers separated by spaces. Print the same numbers from last to first on one line, separated by single spaces. The list can hold a single number, and numbers can repeat or be negative.

Input:

```text
5
1 2 3 4 5
```

Expected output:

```text
5 4 3 2 1
```
hints: The last item of the original list becomes the first item of the new one.
If the list has `n` items, the item at index `i` moves to index `n - 1 - i`.

python.solution:
def reverse_list(nums: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    return nums[::-1]


n = int(input())
nums = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
print(" ".join(str(x) for x in reverse_list(nums)))
